title: Redwood + Mosaic Health - Security & Privacy Review
summary: Security and privacy deep-dive focused on data handling, retention policies, PII/PHI protections, and formal confirmations that customer prompts are not used for model training. Redwood reviewed SOC2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO options, audit logging primitives, KMS integrations, and private deployment alternatives.
action_items: Jordan Kim - Send SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 cert snapshot, and security whitepaper by 2026-11-27
Priya Shah - Share architecture diagram showing VPC/private deployment options and audit log format examples by 2026-11-27
Tom Alvarez - Provide Mosaic Health retention policy and any regulatory constraints for PHI by 2026-12-02
Maya Patel - Request sample SSO metadata for SAML integration and preferred IdP by 2026-12-01
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2/ISO docs and encryption/KMS integration guide
Schedule hands-on pilot kick-off (technical onboarding + baseline benchmarking)
Customer to review retention options and confirm acceptable retention window for prompts/content
Follow-up call to finalize DPA and pilot SOW
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Redwood Support), Laura Mendes (Mosaic CISO), Tom Alvarez (Mosaic Head of Platform), Sanjay Rao (Compliance), Maya Patel (Data Privacy)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. Quick heads up on agenda - Priya will walk the security posture, we'll get into data handling and retention, then leave time for Q&A.
[00:18] Laura: Thanks Jordan, yeah want to focus mostly on prompt retention, PHI handling, and a clear statement about training. Also want to understand audit logs and KMS options.
[00:32] Priya: Great, we'll cover those. To start, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we also maintain ISO27001 certification, I have the certs and the SOC2 report we can share - Jordan will drop them after the call.
[00:48] Tom: Good, please send. On training - we've seen vendors that say they might use customer data to improve models; we need an explicit, contractual confirmation you don't train on our data.
[01:05] Jordan: Totally understood. Short answer: Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to train our public models. We have a strict "no-training-on-customer-data" policy for our hosted tenants; any use for quality debugging is controlled, and customers can opt out or disable retention. We'll include the formal language for the DPA.
[01:26] Sanjay: When you say "opt out or disable retention" - what's the default and what are the retention windows? Also where is the data stored?
[01:38] Priya: Default for hosted accounts is 30 days of prompt/log retention for troubleshooting and billing reconciliation; that's configurable. We offer shorter retention windows, and for Dedicated and Private deployments, we can set retention to zero - essentially no prompt storage on Redwood-managed services. For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, data resides in customer-controlled networks.
[02:02] Maya: Are transcripts or request/response pairs encrypted at rest and in transit? What KMS do you support?
[02:12] Alex: Yes, all data in transit uses TLS. At rest we encrypt with AES-256. For hosted customers we manage keys by default in our KMS; we also support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM integrations for Private deployments. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[02:36] Laura: Good. We need to ensure that any PII/PHI is treated appropriately, e.g., redaction recommendations or support for tokenization before it hits your service.
[02:46] Priya: We recommend client-side redaction or tokenization for PHI when possible. We also provide SDK hooks and middleware examples to strip or hash sensitive fields. For customers who need to keep raw content, we can negotiate data handling terms and minimize retention.
[03:06] Tom: How about audit logs - are actions like model selection, call metadata, tokens consumed logged? Who has access?
[03:16] Priya: Audit logs include request metadata, model version, route, timestamp, and the actor (API key or userid). For Dedicated/Private, logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs or stored within the customer's VPC. Access is role-gated via RBAC; only users with auditing privileges can download full logs.
[03:36] Sanjay: Does your RBAC integrate with SSO - SAML or OIDC? We want centralized auth.
[03:44] Jordan: Yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and OIDC, SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle, and customizable roles. We'll share a sample role mapping for typical platform and admin roles.
[03:58] Maya: For compliance attestation, do you provide audit evidence for things like key rotation and access reviews?
[04:07] Alex: For SOC2 audits we maintain records of key rotation, privileged access reviews, and change logs. We can provide redacted evidence and a list of logs that map to those controls as part of the security pack.
[04:20] Laura: Ok, question on data residency - our data must stay in EMEA. Can you run in-region?
[04:27] Priya: Absolutely. Hosted offerings include region controls; we have deployments in EU regions. For stricter controls we recommend Dedicated capacity in region or Private deployment.
[04:36] Tom: For the "no training" clause, will that be explicit in the DPA? We need legal sign-off.
[04:45] Jordan: Yes, DPA will contain explicit language that customer content won't be used to train models or improve public model weights. We'll provide a standard clause and are open to amendments.
[04:56] Sanjay: Any chance of accidental inclusion of customer data in general telemetry or usage metrics?
[05:02] Alex: Telemetry is aggregated and PII is hashed or removed. We have scrubbing pipelines and reviewers are bound by NDA when needed for debugging. We also provide an option to disable telemetry for certain accounts.
[05:18] Laura: Can you talk about deletion workflows? If we ask to delete all stored prompts for an account, what's the SLA?
[05:26] Priya: For hosted customers, deletion requests are typically processed within 72 hours and we purge backups according to our backup retention schedule; for Dedicated/Private we can implement immediate retention-by-policy. We'll include exact timelines in the DPA.
[05:46] Tom: Are there examples of customers in healthcare with similar controls? We need references or case studies.
[05:53] Jordan: We have several healthcare customers on Dedicated and Private deployments; we'll include anonymized references and relevant case studies in the packet.
[06:02] Maya: On PII detection - do you offer any automated PII detection or labeling on input so we can route sensitive prompts to different handling?
[06:12] Priya: We have a policy engine that can tag requests based on regex/patterns and custom classifiers; we can route flagged traffic to a dedicated tenant with stricter retention and logging. That's commonly used by healthcare customers.
[06:28] Sanjay: What about model variants? If you have a locally hosted fine-tuned model, is there a risk of cross-customer leakage?
[06:36] Priya: Our serving runtime isolates model weights per-deployment and enforces tenancy boundaries. For Dedicated/Private there's physical isolation; for hosted we use multi-tenant pods but isolate KV caches and request handling. We can provide architecture slides showing isolation at the network and process level.
[06:58] Tom: One more, about backups - are backups encrypted and where are they stored?
[07:05] Alex: Backups are encrypted with customer or Redwood-managed keys and stored in region-specific object stores; access is limited to our security ops with justification and audit trail.
[07:18] Laura: Ok that's helpful. We need to finalize a retention window - 30 days default might be too long for PHI. We may need 7 days or zero retention for PHI-bearing routes.
[07:29] Jordan: Understandable. We can scope the pilot to ensure PHI routes have zero retention and telemetry disabled. We'll document config and run tests.
[07:40] Maya: Also want to confirm that any logs we forward to SIEM won't contain raw prompt text unless explicitly configured.
[07:48] Priya: Correct - by default logs contain metadata only; forwarding raw content is opt-in and restricted.
[07:58] Tom: For encryption keys, do you support customer key rotation schedules?
[08:03] Alex: Yes, with CMK customers can rotate per their policy and we maintain key rotation logs. For HSM we can integrate an external signing workflow.
[08:15] Laura: Great. Can you provide sample DPA language now or will it be after sales?
[08:21] Jordan: We'll include a recommended DPA clause as part of the packet. If legal wants edits we can iterate.
[08:29] Sanjay: Are you ISO 27017/27018 compliant or just ISO27001?
[08:34] Priya: Currently ISO27001; we also follow privacy best practices aligned with 27018 controls and can map our controls to those standards for your review.
[08:48] Maya: Ok thanks. Anything else on monitoring or anomaly detection for exfil attempts?
[08:55] Alex: We have monitoring for abnormal API patterns, spike detection, and can generate alerts. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with customer SIEM for real-time alerts.
[09:08] Jordan: Sounds like a good place to wrap. Quick recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO/whitepaper, KMS integration guide, architecture slides, role mapping, and the DPA draft. Action items will be in the notes.
[09:26] Laura: Thanks, let's plan pilot scope with zero retention for PHI routes and a 7-day window for non-PHI, pending legal review.
[09:36] Jordan: Perfect, we'll follow up with proposed pilot SOW and schedule the kickoff.
[09:42] Tom: Thanks all, appreciate it.
[09:45] End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and minor transcription errors ("KV cash" etc.) due to background noise.
